The *Vedagūpañha* ("The Question on the One Who Knows") is a section of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 3.3.6) [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the dialogue between King Milinda and the monk Nāgasena. Four modern translations in three languages are recorded on SuttaCentral, including an English translation by John Kelly [SuttaCentral].
In comparative literature, SuttaCentral registers a full Chinese parallel to this dialogue in T 1670b at section 2.28, titled "Is there a Soul?" [SuttaCentral]. The text displays substantial reuse across early and late Pali literature; DharmaNexus identifies 238 matching passages across 21 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its segments (particularly §7.2–7.3) share notable textual formulas with canonical collections such as the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), the *Sunakkhatta Sutta* (MN 105), and the *Chachakka Sutta* (MN 148) [DharmaNexus]. Internally, repeated dialogue formulas link it to other *Milindapañha* discussions, including Mil 3.3.5 (*Bhavantasaṅkhārajāyamānapañha*), Mil 6.3.6 (*Akālamaraṇapañha*), and Mil 3.4.5 (*Vāyāmakaraṇapañha*) [DharmaNexus]. Shared passages also appear in post-canonical commentarial and Abhidhamma manuals, such as the *Abhidhammāvatāra* and Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. Across languages, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text (§4.6–4.8) with the Sarvāstivāda Sanskrit *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus].
